## The Numbers Tell the Story

Let's cut straight to the data: 12 wins, 2 losses, 85.7% accuracy on September 27th. This is what happens when the model clicks. I've broken down every single pick, every probability, and what the numbers reveal about our methodology.

## Performance by Confidence Level

Here's what the distribution looks like. Our highest confidence pick was Cubs at 61%, and even our lowest at 50% hit. The two misses? Rays at 54% and Guardians at 61% - proving that even 60%+ probabilities aren't guarantees.

content.value:
## Game-by-Game Breakdown

Every prediction, every percentage point, laid out. Notice how our 50-59% probability range went 7-1, while the 60%+ tier went 3-1. The data shows strong performance across all confidence brackets.

## Key Statistical Observations

**Confidence vs. Accuracy:** Our 61% probability picks went 3-2 (60% actual accuracy). The 54% picks? 1-1 exactly. This variance reinforces why we focus on long-term performance over single-day samples.

**Best Calls:** The Nationals pick at 50-50 odds hitting shows even our closest calls had merit. The Cubs, Dodgers, and Mariners all delivered as projected in the 59-61% range.

**The Misses:** Rays at 54% and Guardians at 61% both fell short. No excuses - these are data points that improve the model's learning curve.
